model_classes.about: The Leaderboard's Class keys (Ümit, bus #4217, one scale on the Reading and Logic & Math sites; sitebuild/leaderboard.py, Site.model_class): an open model (released weights: its size record counts the released checkpoint or cites its Hugging Face page, Site.is_open) with a disclosed size by its TOTAL parameters as the size record gives it (export_results.py SIZES; Gemma's E models by their total with embeddings); a closed model, or an open one whose maker discloses no size, by its list price per 1M input tokens, the base rate (Site.list_price: prices here, else results.json prices, the runner's PRICES). Each scale's classes in order, each up to and including its max, the last with none. small_models.left_out_models are in no class and show under Class: All only; a model with neither a disclosed size nor a per-token list price is Undisclosed (Ümit #4259), its key last and hidden while empty. prices: the standard list input rate (Ümit #4238: never an introductory or promotional one) where results.json has none for the model ID, more than one, or a promotional one (model ID: input, source, date, why; provisional where only an introductory or promotional price is published, which marks the class provisional).
model_classes.line: Size by total parameters, as disclosed by the maker (for MoE models the label also shows active parameters): Tiny under 6B · Small 6B–15B · Medium over 15B up to 40B · Large over 40B. Models of undisclosed size, by standard list price per 1M input tokens: Efficient up to $0.50 · Workhorse up to $3 · Flagship over $3.

display_names.about: Every page shows a setup by its model's official name only, with a small tag beside it for how we ran it, setting · route · snapshot (the project lead's rule, Ümit #4445; the three sites' scheme, #4449; sitebuild/names.py). results.json keeps each run's setup name, run id and model id unchanged. The names, their source status ('maker', 'inferred', 'openrouter-only', 'unverified': not every name is maker-proven), snapshots and base models come from the three sites' shared table, model_names.json at the site's root (logic #4487, #4510, #4514, #4517, copied byte for byte), by model_key, or by a row's source_model_key where Reading's key differs from the shared one (the one alias, used for the name and for All benches' join; Reading's own files keep its model_key). Here only what the table lacks and Reading's tag rules. pending: by setup name, the name shown for a model the table does not carry yet whose setup name carries a note (none today). routes: by run id, a decision model's route where two of its setups differ by it (named, never inferred; 'with web' follows from the run). snapshots: by model ID, a release the table lacks (none today), the tag's last part.

method_records.about: Numbers the method and limits sections state that neither results.json nor answers.json holds. Each group names where it was recorded; build_page.py checks the key review against results.json's excluded questions.

api.cost_basis: Estimated from published prices and recorded token usage

subscription.cost_basis: Subscription run priced as if we had used the API

free.cost_basis: Free tier used; estimated at the list price for the same model

local.cost_basis: No dollar estimate; see hardware and time

first_cost_marks.about: A saving whose first model ran on our own hardware, by how its cost was counted: 'local' (no estimate; the cost is left out) and 'maker' (the maker's list price for the same model). The marker after the saving, its tooltip, and the note under the table (shown after the marker, and only when the marker is in the table). The 'maker' marker also follows such a model's own cost. 'upper' marks, before the value, every cost that is an upper-bound estimate (a run's cost_upper_bound: web grounding's search fee counted for every request), with its note wherever such a cost shows. 'weights' and 'gpu' (no marker) explain the two other estimates of a setup on our hardware, by its cost_basis: a public host's list price for the same weights, and the run's GPU time at a public on-demand price per GPU-hour; a cost tooltip gives the tip, and a list showing such a cost gives the note once.

local.tip: Leaves out the first model’s hardware cost, which we have not estimated.
local.note: Leaves out the first model’s hardware cost, which we have not estimated.

maker.tip: Counts the first model at its maker’s list price for the same model; our hardware cost is not measured.
maker.note: Counts the first model at its maker’s list price for the same model; our hardware cost is not measured.

upper.tip: Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.
upper.note: Upper-bound estimate: one $0.001 web search counted per request; Perplexity bills only completed searches.

weights.tip: Estimated at a public host's list price for the same weights, from our recorded tokens; it ran on our GPUs, so this is an API-equivalent estimate, not what it cost us.
weights.note: On our GPUs, estimated at a public host's list price for the same weights (the host, the date read and any precision difference are on each setup's page): an API-equivalent estimate, not measured spending.

gpu.tip: Estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026). A cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending.
gpu.note: On our GPUs with no public price for the same weights, estimated from GPU time: the run's request time x the GPUs its server held x Runpod's on-demand price for an RTX PRO 6000, $2.49 per GPU-hour (read 5 November 2026): a cloud-equivalent estimate, not measured spending.

rank_scale.about: The colours of a decision model's bar in the single-series charts of the Hallucination, Page images and Artificial Analysis pages, from the worst decision model on the chart to the best: dark blue, turquoise, green, yellow. The Topics heat map and the link preview use the same colours. The home page's charts, English reading and English and Turkish colour each setup by its model family (model_families).

model_families.about: Each setup's model family, whose colour its bar or dot takes in the charts of the home page (Turkish reading and grammar, every model group), English reading and English and Turkish: a maker's line of models shares one colour, in every chart and in both model groups. A run belongs to its family by provider and, where one provider serves several families, by model; the build stops unless every run belongs to exactly one. Each family's maker and colour come from maker_colours.json, the one colour map of the three benchmark sites (kept by the Logic & Math site and copied here unchanged), which lists every maker's families; the build stops unless exactly one maker lists each family. Beside each setup's name, its family's icon: the maker's official mark, drawn in the text colour, where the family names one (icon, a Simple Icons slug in sitebuild/family_icons.py), otherwise a plain shape on the family's colour.

leaderboard.about: The Leaderboard's rows (sitebuild/leaderboard.py): one row per model ID, kind (chat or decision model) and web search, at the model's highest reasoning setting, never its best score. Each family's maker (model_families[].maker) is the organisation the site names for it on the Method and model pages, else the family's name. dated_checkpoints groups a dated checkpoint's setups under its original model's row (the row shows the original; the checkpoint's setups sit under its other settings); only this map groups model IDs, never similar names.

not_run.name: SubQ Snap Preview
not_run.reason: Not run: SubQ's API returns its probabilities in 32-bit precision, so their sums miss our 7-decimal check. An allowance for that was approved on 5 November 2026 for its English runs; a Turkish run with “Bilmiyorum” was not part of that request.
Perplexity's API now answers requests for v1.1 with v1.2, so a new run could not measure v1.1.

since 10 October, our requests for fastino/GLiDE have been answered by Fastino's glide_v2 engine, not the glide engine of its Turkish run (6 October), so an English run would not measure the same model.
their first-release weights are no longer on our disk (the server folder now holds the 1017 weights), so a run needs them downloaded again first.

turkish_running.about: English-only setups whose Text tab run is still running, by model id: their Turkish side reads Running, not Not run, until the run is in (the project lead via Zeki #4748: a measure still running is shown pending, never as 0 or another run's number). The build stops when a listed model is not an English-only setup.

method_notes: Perplexity Decider 27B v1.2 (its setup tagged DGX Spark), Perplexity Decider Flash v1.2 and Fastino GLiDE v1.2 made their Text tab runs on an NVIDIA DGX Spark and their English runs on our RTX PRO 6000 GPU, with the same checkpoint, server code and settings.
Celeris-1 Decision was added on 3 November 2026 with one English run, although its repeated Turkish runs changed answers, for which the rule under Runs gives five.

SubQ Snap Preview's English runs (5 November 2026) returned the same choices and probabilities as SubQ Snap 1.1's English run (2 November 2026) on all 547 questions, and every response named the Preview model. Its Turkish run (13 October 2026) and SubQ Snap 1.1's (1 November 2026) differ on 519 of 2,198 questions. The model behind each name was not verified; read SubQ Snap Preview's Turkish against English comparison with this in mind.

structural_check.about: runner/translate_reading.py check on the final translations: the questions with a problem (a missing translation, the option letters, an empty text or the underline markup) and the number of warnings (numbering, numbers, Turkish letters, length). The build stops unless every problem question is flagged.

all_benches.about: All benches (sitebuild/all_benches.py), at url, outside this site (built into _suite/all-benches/; its earlier address all-benches/ redirects there). benches: the other sites' published bench-scores.json files, one bench each (bench: its id in the file), read by the build (the page shows a bench only once its file is live); a bench with parts (logic-math: logic and math, Ümit #4234) is shown in their place until all its parts are live, and the Combined score uses it either way. their_score: the Jev Decision Index's own score for its 15 open decision models, a sanity check beside ours, never shown as our score; joined to our rows by Hugging Face repo, the reference by model_key. training: the training method as a small tag beside a model's name, only where our setup records state it (export_results.py MODELS notes and SIZES scopes), by repo or, for a model without one, by name. latency_runs: the Text tab runs timed on the pinned machine (spark2, a DGX Spark GB10; one request at a time), by the host in the answer store's runs.ollama_url, not the hardware text (both of our DGX Sparks read the same); a model with none reads 'not timed on the pinned machine yet'. not_combined: rows a combined score would join although one model did not answer every bench (a hosted service that changed its model between the benches' runs), matched as the page joins rows (repo, else model_key and kind, never by name); each keeps its per-bench scores, gets no combined score, and the combined board shows its reason.

aliases.about: Rows of another site's bench that name a model differently from this site's rows, by bench key and the row's name as the file gives it: the model_key of this site's row it joins (Ümit #4270, #4277). Used where the row's own model_key joins no model; the row keeps its scores, the model this site's name.
